clips.text: There goes the last clean breath of Town air. All right, mountain. Let's see what you've been keeping.
The light changes this far down. It stops following you and starts waiting to see if you'll turn back.
So this is where the easy part ends. Good. I was starting to distrust how friendly the entrance looked.
Town is still above me, but it already sounds like a memory. Pick steady, feet steady. That's enough.
The walls are colder than they should be. Not empty, though. Nothing this quiet is ever truly empty.
One step under the safe line, and every sound belongs to the cave. Mine too, now. Keep moving.
There it is. The pick, the stone, the next breath—all landing where they should.
Don't rush it. The wall is giving way because the rhythm is clean, not because I'm hitting harder.
Every strike is finding the last one's weakness. Keep the line moving before the stone catches up.
Hands are moving faster than the doubt now. That's usually when the good tunnels open.
I've been swinging long enough to forget the first wall. The mountain hasn't forgotten me, though.
At this pace, either the tunnel ends first or my shoulders file a formal complaint.
Wait. That colour isn't from the lantern. Easy now—I want the whole seam to come out breathing.
I've seen stone pretend to be valuable before. This isn't pretending. I can feel it through the handle.
There you are. Same quiet shine, same stubborn grip on the rock. I remember how to free you.
The deeper ones always look untouched, like the mountain believed distance would be enough to protect them.
That vein is holding its own light. For once, I don't mind the dark showing me where to look.
Another piece that doesn't belong with the rock around it. Makes me wonder who decided where it did belong.
Easy, little Star. You've been buried longer than I've been alive. Take a moment before you meet the sky.
There you are. Stone can hold the light for an age, but it never teaches the light to stop wanting out.
That one changed the whole room when it opened its eyes. I think even the shadows stepped back.
You waited all the way down here and still remembered how to shine. Come on. I'll carry the first part.
The light bends differently around this one. Beautiful, yes—but beauty and safety stopped being relatives down here.
Another passenger for the walk home. At least Stars travel light, even when they make the whole pack glow.
That is no statue. The stone is breathing around it, as though the entire chamber is trying not to wake it.
I thought the old miners made them larger with every telling. They were trying to make the truth fit inside a story.
Another one. Different face, same silence pressing against my ribs. The mountain remembers its guardians.
Look at the floor around its feet. Those aren't cracks from age. It moved once, and the chamber learned the shape of it.
Its eyes are closed, but I don't feel unobserved. Let's show some respect and keep our tools quiet.
Every Titan makes the tunnels feel less abandoned. Not safer. Just less empty than I wanted to believe.
The cavern is turning blue ahead. Keep the lantern steady; every reflection is hiding another passage.
Feel that warmth in the wall? The Amber Depths aren't sleeping. They're listening through the stone.
The echoes disappear here instead of coming back. I don't know what the crystals do with them.
Silver in the rock, silver in the dust, silver on my gloves. We've crossed into the old workings.
The stone is warm enough to breathe against us. This is the Core. From here on, the mountain gets a vote.
I know this change in the air. New ground, old rules: watch the ceiling, trust the pick, leave a road home.
That's farther than the last marker. Doesn't look like much from here, but Town would feel the difference.
Another marker behind us. I like progress better when it leaves a tunnel I can walk back through.
We're deep enough that the surface feels borrowed from somebody else's life. Still, the air reaches us.
The number on the marker keeps growing. So does the road home. I intend to use both.
A respectable depth, according to the sign. My knees have submitted a less flattering report.
Every hundred metres, the dark becomes a little more honest about how far it goes.
That's new ground beneath my boots. The old deepest point is somewhere above us now.
Past the old mark again. Funny how yesterday's limit looks like part of the road once you're below it.
No map of mine reaches this far. From here on, every safe step is a piece of the next one.
A personal best. I'd celebrate louder, but the ceiling has been taking an unhealthy interest in us.
I've never stood this far beneath the sky. I can still picture it, which feels important.
The mountain moved the line again, and I followed. Not forever. Just farther than before.
That tremor was the warning. Get clear of the loose ceiling and move when the dust moves.
Here it comes again. Leave the ore, watch the marked ground, and keep a clean path behind you.
Hear that crack travelling above us? The deep rock is passing the danger from chamber to chamber.
The floor is rolling left. Don't fight it—step with it, then clear the fracture before it answers back.
The mountain just took a breath. We do not want to be under it when it lets go.
I know this sound now, and I hate that I know it. Open ground, quickly. The stones are choosing where to fall.
Still standing. Give the dust a moment to settle before we trust any ceiling it reveals.
The silence after a quake is always too polite. Like the mountain expects thanks for stopping.
That collapse opened a passage. Useful doesn't mean friendly, but I won't pretend I'm not curious.
That one came close enough to shake the confidence out of my hands. They'll settle. They always do.
Nothing broken that wasn't already stone. I'll call that a successful disagreement with the mountain.
Down here, a quake doesn't sound loud. It sounds enormous, which is somehow worse.
The dark is getting inside the rhythm of my breathing. Light first, distance second. Pride can wait.
Not this feeling again. Find the lantern's edge and stay inside it until my hands remember they're mine.
Too fast. The floor is arriving before I can read it. Slow the descent or the cave will choose the landing.
Pressure's climbing behind my eyes. No heroics now. A living miner can come back for stubborn ore.
One clear decision at a time: light the route, leave the wall, keep moving toward air.
I'm afraid. Good. Fear still knows where the exit is. Let it point, then make the feet follow.
There. My breathing belongs to me again. Let's not spend it all at once.
The pressure's easing. I can feel the shape of the room instead of only the way out.
Funny what a little honest light can do. The same walls, the same depth, and suddenly I fit inside myself again.
That Star's light reaches somewhere the lantern can't. The shaking stopped before I noticed.
Crisis postponed. I'd call that rest, but my shoulders are laughing at the idea.
The deep still feels heavy. It just doesn't feel heavier than me right now.
The pack's nearly closed. One careful choice now, or the next good find stays where we found it.
If I add another crystal, this bag becomes part of the architecture. We need a merchant.
Plenty worth carrying, not much room left to carry it. Greed gets heavier before the pack does.
Long road home, full pack, deeper tunnel ahead. The sensible answer is obvious. I resent it already.
No more maybes. Keep what matters, leave what doesn't, and remember the route back to the rest.
The straps are telling the truth before I do: we're carrying enough to make the return worthwhile.
Fresh air. I almost forgot it had a taste. We came back lighter on supplies and heavier with stories.
Town lights again. They look smaller every time I leave and brighter every time I make it back.
We brought the Stars home. The rest of the haul can wait; light like that deserves the first welcome.
Made it back. Don't ask how close the last tunnel came. I haven't decided which version I can admit to.
Good weight in the pack and ground under the boots that remembers sunlight. That's a proper return.
Same Town, same gate, different miner coming through it. The deep always keeps a small piece of the one who entered.
That's not decoration. That's a promise to the next wall, and I intend to make it keep the promise.
Good steel costs because bad steel waits until you're deep enough to trust it. This was the right choice.
More reach in the sky and another way home from below. Strange how the same power can promise both.
I can feel the Gem Power settle differently already. Stronger, yes. That means the mistakes get stronger too.
There goes most of the wallet. If the next expedition goes well, I'll call it foresight instead of impulse.
This opens ground I couldn't survive yesterday. Give me a minute to respect that before I go looking for it.
Real warmth, not heat leaking through stone. I'd forgotten the difference.
Same fire, different dust on the boots. It never asks how deep I went before it lets me sit.
The deep is still humming in my bones. Give the flames a moment; they know how to answer.
I came back with less courage than I left with. That's all right. Courage grows back near a fire.
Five minutes here and I'll be ready to make questionable decisions underground again.
Firelight and Starlight don't look alike, but they make the same promise: you don't have to sit in the dark alone.
